discovery: Atom interferometry with matter waves and its development into a precision tool for inertial sensing and fundamental physics

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: CNRS / Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Université Sorbonne Paris Nord, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum sensing
motivation: Bordé showed that Ramsey-type laser spectroscopy is a matter-wave interferometer; in 1991 Pritchard's group built the first atom interferometer with material gratings, and Kasevich (with Chu) demonstrated light-pulse atom interferometry and used it to measure gravity. Kasevich then turned it into gyroscopes, gradiometers and precision tests. Atom interferometers now give some of the best measurements of the fine-structure constant, sensitive tests of the equivalence principle, measurements of Newton's G, and limits on dark energy and ultralight dark matter. Long-baseline instruments such as MAGIS-100 and AION are being built to search for dark matter and to detect mid-band gravitational waves. This work combines deep quantum physics with experimental engineering. It opened a new field of quantum sensing that serves particle physics, cosmology, geodesy and navigation. It is a clear example of quantum technology being used to answer fundamental questions.
